title: Upper Bounded Wildcards (? extends T) & Covariance
summary: Master <? extends T>: reading elements safely as type T, preventing adding elements (except null), and covariance in method parameters.
prerequisites: Bounded Type Parameters: Enforcing Upper Bounds
learningObjectives: Master the upper bounded wildcard syntax: List<? extends T>
Understand covariance: enabling flexible polymorphic reads across subclass collections
Analyze why writing elements to a <? extends T> collection is strictly prohibited by the compiler
Recognize the Producer role in API design: using ? extends T when collections produce data
expectedOutcomes: Ability to design flexible, covariant read-only API method signatures in production
Clear understanding of why write prohibition guarantees total heap type safety

activities.title: Practical Context: Digital Audio Streaming Player

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Digital Audio Streaming Player
analogy.story:
Consider a digital audio player library containing a playlist of audio tracks: `Playlist<? extends AudioTrack>`. The player can accept a playlist of MP3Track, FLACLosslessTrack, or PodcastEpisodeTrack.

The audio player's decoding engine reads tracks sequentially and streams them to the speakers (`track.playPcmStream()`). Because every track is guaranteed to be at least an `AudioTrack`, playback succeeds with zero type casting.

However, the player is not allowed to insert a new `WavTrack` into the playlist during playback: the playlist might be a specialized `Playlist<FLACLosslessTrack>`, and inserting an uncompressed WAV would corrupt the user's high-res audio library.
analogy.keyTakeaway: Upper bounded wildcards (? extends T) make collections read-safe providers (producers). You can read elements as type T, but you cannot insert elements into them.

activities.title: Covariance with <? extends T>: Read Safety & Write Prohibition

keyTakeaways: Upper bounded wildcards (? extends T) introduce covariance to Java generics
List<? extends Number> accepts List<Integer>, List<Double>, List<Float>, and List<Number>
Elements read from List<? extends T> are guaranteed to be of type T (or subclasses)
Writing any object (except literal null) into List<? extends T> causes a compile-time error
This is the 'P' (Producer) in the PECS principle: Producer Extends

activities.title: Covariant Number Range Aggregator
activities.description: Trace a method aggregating numeric data across diverse List<Integer> and List<Double> instances.

steps.description: Declare calculateSum(List<? extends Number> numbers). This enables covariance: List<Integer> and List<Double> are both accepted.
Read each element as type Number. Calling num.doubleValue() is verified at compile-time.
Both intList and dblList invoke calculateSum cleanly with zero compiler warnings.

questions.question: Given the declaration 'List<? extends Number> list = new ArrayList<Integer>();', which of the following lines will compile without error?
questions.explanation: Because list is declared as List<? extends Number>, the compiler cannot verify what concrete subtype list actually points to (it could be List<Double>). Therefore, no object can be added except null, which is the only universal literal.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a collection parameterized with '<? extends T>' in a method signature?
options: A Consumer that receives newly created elements
A Producer that provides (reads) elements of type T to the method
A Bi-directional cache for reading and writing simultaneously
questions.explanation: In accordance with Joshua Bloch's PECS rule (Producer Extends, Consumer Super), '? extends T' is used when the collection is a Producer—it produces items of type T for your method to read.

activities.title: Senior Engineer Interview: Why Covariant Collections Are Read-Only

qaList.question: Why did Java designers choose to make 'List<? extends T>' strictly read-only with respect to adding elements, and what bug would occur if this restriction were lifted?
qaList.answer: If Java allowed adding elements to 'List<? extends T>', it would destroy the foundation of compile-time type safety. For example, if 'List<? extends Number>' allowed calling 'list.add(10)', and that reference happened to point to a 'List<Double>' created elsewhere, the underlying list would now contain an Integer. When subsequent code reading from 'List<Double>' executed 'Double d = list.get(0)', the JVM would crash with a ClassCastException. By disallowing all writes to '<? extends T>' (except null), Java mathematically guarantees that a collection's contents can never be contaminated by an incompatible sibling type.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I understand how <? extends T> introduces covariance to generic method parameters
I know why List<Integer> can be passed to List<? extends Number>
I understand why the compiler prevents adding elements into a <? extends T> collection
I recognize the Producer role in PECS: Producer Extends

practiceProblems.title: Find Maximum Value in Number Subtype List
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method findMaxAsDouble(List<? extends Number> numbers) that returns the maximum doubleValue() among all elements, or Double.NaN if the list is null or empty.

practiceProblems.title: Count Elements Exceeding Threshold
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method countExceeding(List<? extends Number> numbers, double threshold) that counts how many numbers have doubleValue() strictly greater than threshold.

practiceProblems.title: Sum Even Integers Across Number Providers
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method sumEvenInts(List<? extends Number> numbers) that extracts each number's intValue() and returns the sum of all even integers.

practiceProblems.title: Verify All Numbers Positive
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method areAllPositive(List<? extends Number> numbers) that returns true if all non-null numbers in the list have doubleValue() > 0. Returns true for empty list.

practiceProblems.title: Find First Element With Prefix in String Provider
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method findWithPrefix(List<? extends CharSequence> list, String prefix) that returns the first CharSequence that starts with prefix, or null if none match.
